title: Degreewise relative categories realize enriched localization
statement:
Use simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, object-preserving locally Kan replacements and the derived coherent nerve as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and infinity categories and coherent diagrams as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Enlarge universes to contain all the categories and diagrams below. For a quasicategory $Q$ and a class $S$ of its edges, a localization $Q[S^{-1}]_\infty$ means a quasicategory with a functor $q:Q\to Q[S^{-1}]_\infty$ such that, for every quasicategory $E$, restriction is an equivalence from $\operatorname{Fun}(Q[S^{-1}]_\infty,E)$ to the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_S(Q,E)$ on functors inverting $S$; thus the universal property includes every coherent transformation.

Let $A$ be any small simplicial category. Suppose $B\subseteq A$ is a simplicial subcategory with the same objects and with each $B(x,y)\subseteq A(x,y)$ a union of connected components. Here components are equivalence classes of vertices under finite zigzags of simplicial edges, and a union of components includes every simplex having vertices in those components. No interval objects, saturation of morphisms, or model structure on $A$ is assumed. For $n\geq0$ let $A_n$ be the ordinary category with these objects and morphisms $A(x,y)_n$, with composition induced by simplicial composition; let $B_n$ be its wide subcategory with morphisms $B(x,y)_n$. The simplicial operators make $(A_n,B_n)$ a simplicial diagram of relative ordinary categories. Put $D=\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$ and let $V_B$ be the edges corresponding to vertices in $B(x,y)$.

The localizations in this statement exist. Enriched evaluation induces a natural coherent cocone from $[n]\mapsto N(A_n)[B_n^{-1}]_\infty$ to $D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty$, and its comparison is an equivalence in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$:
$$\operatorname*{colim}_{[n]\in\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}N(A_n)[B_n^{-1}]_\infty\ \simeq\ D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty.$$
The degree-zero leg of this cocone is induced by the actual vertex-category map $N(A_0)\to D$ followed by localization. The comparison is natural for simplicial functors preserving the subcategories $B$, and for changes of the object-preserving locally Kan replacement.

source.place: Notation 1.3.4.11 and Proposition 1.3.4.14, printed pp. 112-113, and the marked homotopy-colimit comparison in the proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp. 113-114. The statement isolates that comparison for an arbitrary union-of-components simplicial subcategory. No Stacks tag states this enriched result.

proof.text:
For every $n$, define $T_nA$ to have the objects of $A$ and mapping simplicial sets $t_n(A(x,y))$ of [lem-coef-join-translation-resolution]. Its composition and identities are those of $A$ in degree $n+m+1$; restriction along ordinal sums commutes with these operations. Thus there are strict simplicial-functor diagrams
$$A_\bullet\xleftarrow{p_\bullet}T_\bullet A\xrightarrow{e_\bullet}\operatorname{const}(A),$$
where an ordinary $A_n$ is discretely enriched. The first-block restrictions give $p_n$, the last-block restrictions give $e_n$. The translation lemma makes every mapping-set map of $p_n$ a weak homotopy equivalence. It is the identity on objects, hence induces an equivalence on $\pi_0$ and is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Consequently $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(p_\bullet)$ is an equivalence of coherent diagrams: each component is an equivalence and the criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applies. This construction works for arbitrary, possibly non-Kan, mapping sets.

source.place: Notation 1.3.4.11, Lemma 1.3.4.12 and first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 1.3.4.14, printed pp.112-113

proof.text: By [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent], geometric realization of simplicial spaces commutes with finite products; thus $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted in the definition of [lem-coef-sifted-fixed-object-hocolimit]. The augmentation $e_\bullet$ is identity on the fixed object set, and [lem-coef-join-translation-resolution] says for every pair $(x,y)$ that its mapping-space cocone is colimiting. Apply the fixed-object criterion to $T_\bullet A\to A$. It gives a colimiting cocone to $D=\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$. Inverting the diagram equivalence $p_\bullet$ of Step 1 gives a coherent colimiting cocone $i_n:N(A_n)\to D$. Perform this inversion in the functor category of diagrams depending on $A$, in an enlarged universe: $p_\bullet$ is itself natural in $A$, and the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says it is an equivalence in that functor category. A functor equivalence has an inverse there, so this supplies a coherently natural cocone. To identify its zero-degree map, let $c_0:A_0\to T_0A$ send a vertex arrow to its completely degenerate simplices. Then $p_0c_0=1$, while $e_0c_0$ is exactly the inclusion of the vertex category in $A$. Hence $i_0$ is the actual vertex-category map followed by the chosen locally Kan replacement and its coherent nerve. This fixes the zero-degree leg of the cocone, up to its canonical coherent identification.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.14, printed p.113; the two hypotheses in Lemma 1.3.4.10 are checked on the actual translation cocone

proof.text:
We first supply existence of all edge localizations with their entire functor-category universal property. For a quasicategory $Q$ and edges $S$, mark $S$ and the degenerate edges, obtaining $X=(Q,S)$. The functorial marked-anodyne replacement of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] gives $j:X	o L^
atural$. It is a weak equivalence in the model structure of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]: restriction on $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(-,E^
atural)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $E$, as the lifting lemma states. Put $F=\operatorname{Map}^{ lat}(X,E^
atural)$. Directly from the marking definition, $F$ is the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_S(Q,E)$: an $m$-simplex is a map $Q	imes\Delta^m	o E$ inverting each marked arrow at each of its $m+1$ vertices. For any small quasicategory $T$, the cartesian product assertion of the marked-model node makes $T^
atural	imes j$ a weak equivalence. The defining weak-equivalence test therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(L,E))^\simeq\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Fun}(T,F)^\simeq.$$
Indeed both sides are the corresponding $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}$ into $E^
atural$: an equivalence of $T$ is carried to a componentwise equivalence, which is an equivalence of functor categories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Taking all $T$ proves the equivalence of the two functor categories: for the restriction functor $u:U	o F$, the test $T=F$ lifts $1_F$ to a right inverse $v$, and full faithfulness on the test mapping space with $T=U$ identifies $vu$ with $1_U$ because $uvu$ is identified with $u$. This proves $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)\simeq F$, through restriction along $j$. This constructs the required localization functorially, including every coherent transformation. The marking on $Q$ need not be saturated or satisfy two-out-of-three. Apply it to $(N(A_n),B_n)$ and to $(D,V_B)$.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.2, printed p.108; HTT Section 3.1, via the cited marked-model and marked-anodyne statements; full-functor verification written out here

proof.text: Check exactly which arrows the unmarked cocone of Step 2 inverts. For a fixed $n$, there is a simplicial functor $c_n:A_n\to T_nA$, induced in mapping degree $m$ by the monotone map $[n+m+1]\to[n]$ that fixes $0,\ldots,n$ and sends all of the last block to $n$. It preserves composition and has $p_nc_n=1$. Consequently the $n$th cocone map $i_n$ is coherently equivalent to $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(e_nc_n)$, and $e_nc_n$ sends an arrow $b\in A(x,y)_n$ to its final vertex $b|_{\{n\}}$. No naturality of $c_n$ in $n$ is asserted or needed: the coherent cocone comes from the natural span in Step 1. If $b\in B_n$, its final vertex lies in $B(x,y)_0$, so this arrow of $D$ belongs to $V_B$. Thus any $F:D\to E$ inverting $V_B$ has every $Fi_n$ inverting $B_n$. Conversely, if every $Fi_n$ inverts $B_n$, the case $n=0$ and the identified zero-degree leg imply that $F$ inverts $V_B$. These conditions are invariant under coherent equivalence of functors by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The union-of-components hypothesis ensures the marking is also unchanged by replacing a vertex with any homotopic representative: both the first-block vertices and the last-block vertex of any simplex lie in one component, and local Kan replacement preserves these components by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp.113-114: the markings W_n and their preimages on T_n; the comparison uses only the stated union-of-components property

proof.text: For completeness the passage from colimits to entire functor categories follows from the cartesian closedness and small colimits in [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout]. If $C=\operatorname{colim}_n C_n$, test the canonical map $\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)\to\lim_n\operatorname{Fun}(C_n,E)$ by mapping out of any $T$. Cartesian closedness makes $T\times-$ a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits. The mapping-space criterion for colimiting cocones of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to $T\times C=\operatorname{colim}_n(T\times C_n)$ gives the equivalence on these test mapping spaces, hence the claimed equivalence of infinity categories. Now put $L_n=N(A_n)[B_n^{-1}]_\infty$ using the functorial construction of Step 3, and let $P=\operatorname{colim}_n L_n$, which exists by the same node. The functorial localization universal property and Step 4 give a coherent cocone $L_\bullet\to D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty$, induced by the unmarked cocone, and thus its comparison $h:P\to D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty$. Its degree-zero leg is the localization of the actual map identified in Step 2.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp.113-114, marked homotopy-colimit comparison; internal-Hom form of the colimit universal property written out

proof.text:
Apply Steps 3 and 5, retaining the restriction maps, to obtain
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)\simeq\lim_n\operatorname{Fun}(L_n,E)\simeq\lim_n\operatorname{Fun}_{B_n}(N(A_n),E).$$
The unmarked cocone of Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Fun}(D,E)\simeq\lim_n\operatorname{Fun}(N(A_n),E)$. Under this equivalence the last displayed limit is precisely the full subcategory on compatible objects whose $n$th component inverts $B_n$: fullness can be checked by testing a coherent diagram of any shape $T$, since a map $T\to\operatorname{Fun}_{B_n}(N(A_n),E)$ is exactly a map to the full ambient functor category with all vertex objects in that subcategory. Thus the compatible transformations and all their higher simplices are retained, not just the cores. By Step 4 this is the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_{V_B}(D,E)$, and by Step 3 it is $\operatorname{Fun}(D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty,E)$. All these maps are restriction along the chosen cocones, so their composite is $h^*$. It follows that $h$ is an equivalence: using $E=P$ gives a left inverse, and using $E=D[V_B^{-1}]_\infty$ and full faithfulness of restriction gives the other inverse identity. This proves the displayed comparison with its specified cocone.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp.113-114: expand the marked-colimit step as a universal-property argument on full functor categories

proof.text: Every ordinal-sum restriction in Step 1 commutes with a simplicial functor $A\to A'$; if it preserves $B$, the conditions on marked vertices in Step 4 commute as well. The functorial marked replacements of Step 3 and the colimit construction therefore supply the asserted natural comparisons. For a change of object-preserving locally Kan replacement compatible with the replacement maps from $A$, the triangle with those maps and two-out-of-three show that the comparison is a weak equivalence on each mapping set, hence a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and an equivalence under the derived coherent nerve by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. It carries the vertex maps to the same vertices and induces an equivalence of the full functor subcategories inverting them; the localization property from Step 3 gives the induced equivalence on localized targets, commuting with their cocones. For two functorial replacements with units $\eta:1\to R$ and $\eta′:1\to R′$, use $RR′A$ as a common refinement. Naturality gives $R(\eta′_A)\eta_A=\eta_{R′A}\eta′_A$. All three unit maps here are weak equivalences on mapping sets, so two-out-of-three makes $R(\eta′_A):RA\to RR′A$ a local weak equivalence. The other leg is $\eta_{R′A}:R′A\to RR′A$, already a local weak equivalence. The displayed equality also proves that this refinement commutes with the original maps from $A$, so it respects the marked vertex maps and the zero-degree cocone leg. For arbitrary choices, the two replacement maps from $A$ already identify both with the same derived object in the homotopy theory of simplicial categories. Hence the comparison is independent of the replacement in the coherent sense asserted, with the degree-zero leg still induced by the actual vertex-category map.

lean.note: The evaluation span is specified on all mapping simplices by the HA join-translation formulas. The localized cocone is induced by this span and is colimiting in the dependency Cat-infinity model; its degree-zero section gives the actual vertex-category leg.
